what_changed_in_this_revision: Agent 2's 882 Atharvavedic HAS_DEVATA_DERIVED edges have ALREADY LANDED in canonical Neo4j (relationships 282,389 -> 283,310). The scope_note defect the lead flagged as a sequencing risk is therefore a LIVE wrong state, not a pending one: 26 DerivedMetric nodes assert a predicate scope that predates those edges. It has not shipped only because no public artifact has been rebuilt since. Step 3 below is a repair, not a precaution.

answer_to_lead_point_2.question: Is your correction a property write, a generator fix, or both?
answer_to_lead_point_2.answer: BOTH, and the generator fix is the one that survives Wave D.

files: src/vedagraph/domain/profiles.py -- attribution_metrics() and corpus_metrics() interpolate the measurement instead of a constant
scripts/build_domain_v2.py -- measures the scope once and passes it to every profile
generator_fix.property: The published sentence is now assembled from a measurement of the whole attribution predicate family taken at generation time. A predicate that gains a corpus widens the sentence with NO prose edit; a predicate that is retired narrows it; an unmeasured build says so rather than falling back on a declaration.

property_write.status: FALLBACK ONLY. Use it if the regeneration in step 3 slips.
property_write.why_not_primary: AGENT6-MUT-01 was a property write. It was applied, and it is already superseded by the 882 edges that landed after it was written. A second write would buy the same short life. Its text is generated by the same function the regeneration uses, so write and regeneration converge on the identical string.

items: src/vedagraph/domain/profiles.py -- ALREADY DONE by Agent 6 (measured scope_note generator).

DO NOT widen ATTRIBUTION_VEDAS to ('RV','AV'). Refused and pinned by a test: the import creates HAS_DEVATA_DERIVED, not HAS_DEVATA, and widening the constant makes 'HAS_DEVATA reaches AV' true in prose while that predicate still has no Atharvavedic edge. Nothing published should read a corpus list out of a constant any more.

insight_service.py predicate widening (HAS_DEVATA|HAS_DEVATA_DERIVED returning the predicate beside the count) -- Agent 2's follow-on, NOT applied by Agent 6. If it lands, set COUNTED_ATTRIBUTION_PREDICATES in profiles.py to match, or the metric's values will widen while its method and scope_note still describe the narrower set.

CRITICAL_TRAP.finding: A regeneration driven by build_domain_v2.py as it stands would fix 25 rows and leave 189 stale.
CRITICAL_TRAP.why: PROFILE_COUNT = 25, and top_devatas() ranks by HAS_DEVATA, which is Rigveda-only -- its own docstring warns that using it to choose what to profile 'builds a Rigvedic top list and calls it a four-Veda one'.
CRITICAL_TRAP.required: Drive the regeneration from the SUBJECT SET OF THE ROWS BEING REPLACED (the union of the 214 staged subject_keys and the 25 live ones), not from top_devatas(PROFILE_COUNT). Verify by re-reading scope_note for every subject in that union, not a sample.

preferred_variant.what: Re-run Agent 2's staging generator (build_agent2_staging.py, which calls attribution_metrics) AFTER step 1, so its 214 rows carry the correct text BEFORE import. Then import.
preferred_variant.why: No wrong row ever lands. metric_id is deterministic, so this is also idempotent against the 25 live nodes.

fallback_variant.what: The lead's provisional order: import the 214 as staged, then regenerate over them.
fallback_variant.why_acceptable: metric_id is deterministic (VG:METRIC:{name}:{subject}), so a regeneration MERGEs over both the staged rows and the live nodes. Safe ONLY if step 3 is a hard gate and no public artifact is built between 2 and 3 -- and only if the subject-set trap above is avoided.

run_in_this_order.verification: Assert that no DerivedMetric.scope_note anywhere in the graph still contains the string 'exists for the Rigveda only'. That is one query and it covers all 214 + 25.

not_exhaustive_caveat.question: Is the removal of the 'not exhaustive' caveat from insight_service.py yours?
not_exhaustive_caveat.measured_basis: The catalogue published 7 cards against 21 benchmark-graded NOT_ANSWERABLE dimensions; it now publishes all 21 with unpublished_not_answerable empty. 'This catalogue is not exhaustive. It records the limits the benchmark graded and probed' had become an understatement of the wrong kind -- it implied the gap was still 7-of-21.
not_exhaustive_caveat.replacement: A measured caveat: it covers every one of the 21 graded NOT_ANSWERABLE questions, each with a probe that runs on request, and the residual is stated precisely -- the benchmark is 100 questions rather than every question, so a question absent from the list is not thereby answerable.
not_exhaustive_caveat.test_updated: tests/api/test_insights.py::test_capability_catalogue_is_enumerable_and_states_its_own_incompleteness now asserts the surviving load-bearing clause 'not thereby answerable' plus unpublished_not_answerable == [], rather than the old wording. Both sentences make the same promise; only that clause is common to them.
not_exhaustive_caveat.why_two_agents_saw_it_red: They ran against a tree from before the test edit landed. It passes now.
